page: Microsoft Azure D4pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with a reduced memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on Microsoft Azure's Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance runs on an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs corresponding to 4 physical cores with a single thread per core. The processor allocation includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is present via AES instructions, whereas x86-specific SIMD instruction sets such as AVX and AMX are naturally omitted.

The VM features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring attached network storage such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems. In synthetic memory bandwidth testing, the instance achieved a read throughput of 86.05 GB/sec and a write throughput of 37.12 GB/sec for large 256 MB blocks, along with a small-block cached read speed of 454.2 GB/sec.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive performance in compression and standard system workloads, highlighted by a single-threaded gzip throughput of 33.08 GB/sec placing in the top quartile. General computing tests show average results, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 5,537.0 and stress-ng multi-core scoring 8,245.96. Network and server evaluations reflect standard baseline metrics, delivering 7.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 8.24 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Synthetic instruction tests like PassMark CPU and encryption, as well as AI inference tasks, reveal limitations common to reduced-instruction ARM architectures lacking specialized matrix extensions.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D4pls_v6 offers strong compute-to-cost efficiency for workloads that do not demand large in-memory capacities. It is well aligned with horizontally scaled web serving, software compilation, CI/CD runners, network proxies, and microservices that prioritize dedicated physical core compute over dense RAM allocation.
description: Microsoft Azure D4pls_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine powered by a 4-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), the instance delivers consistent single-threaded and multi-core performance across standard computing workloads. It lacks onboard local storage and hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-threaded gzip compression performance at 33.08 GB/sec alongside solid multi-core execution in software compilation and static web delivery reaching 7.93 GB/sec. However, raw vector instruction tests and machine learning inference show reduced throughput compared to specialized architectures. The D4pls_v6 provides a cost-effective, compute-dense footprint suitable for CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, web hosting, and lightweight network application layers.
